title: Constraint-aware partial-order task decomposition for multi-agent workflows
research_question: Can a constraint-aware partial-order task decomposition strategy improve end-to-end success rate and reduce coordination overhead in multi-agent workflows compared with fixed sequential decomposition?
hypothesis: Explicitly modeling task dependencies, resource constraints, and opportunities for parallel execution in a partial-order decomposition will yield higher workflow success and lower token/latency cost than fixed sequential or verifier-only decomposition baselines.
motivation: The knowledge base shows repeated rejected ideas around routing, replanning, communication gating, and verifier-guided decomposition, suggesting this area is active but crowded. A clearer gap is the lack of proposals centered on partial-order, constraint-aware decomposition itself: existing rejected ideas mention adaptive or hierarchical decomposition, but not explicit dependency graphs that let agents execute independent subproblems in parallel while respecting constraints. This targets a core bottleneck in agent orchestration—coordination cost grows when workflows are forced into linear plans even when tasks are only partially ordered.
